intro: The main manuscript, joined from many fragments, of Muršili II's 'First Plague Prayer', addressed to the whole assembly of the gods who witnessed the oath. Muršili reports that oracles have named the murder of Tudḫaliya the Younger — the sworn lord whom his father and the Hittite nobility killed, breaking their oath — as the cause of the twenty-year plague; he pleads his own innocence and offers compensation from his own house.

paras.en: Gods, my lords, all the male [gods], all the female gods, all the gods [of the lan]d of Ḫatti; all the male gods of the oath, all the female gods of the oath; the gods of old, all the male gods (and) all the female gods; you gods who on that day were summoned to assembly, to oath (and) to witness; mountains, rivers, springs and underground watercourses (KASKAL.KUR): see, I, Muršili, your priest, your servant, have made a plea to you. And (as for) the matter concerning which I am making a plea to you — gods, my lords, my word […].

Gods, my lords, a plague has arisen in the land of Ḫatti, and the land of Ḫatti has been oppressed by the plague; it has been badly damaged. And because this is the twentieth year that there has been much dying in the land of Ḫatti, the matter of Tudḫaliya the Younger, son of Tudḫaliya, weighed upon me, and I made it the subject of an oracle inquiry to the god; and the matter of Tudḫaliya the Younger was also confirmed by the god. Because Tudḫaliya the Younger was their lord for the land of Ḫatti, the princes, the lords, the commanders of thousands, the dignitaries, the troops and [chario]try of [Ḫat]tuša — all of them — had sworn (an oath) to him; and my father too had sworn to him.

But my father went and wronged Tudḫaliya. The land of Ḫattuša — the princes, the lords, the commanders of thousands (and) the dignitaries, all of them — sided with my father, and they rebelled against Tudḫaliya, their sworn lord, and killed him. Moreover, as for the brothers he had, […]-uda and Pirwa, they seized them and sent(?) them to the land of Alašiya. And because Tudḫaliya was their lord, and they had been his sworn servants, they broke your oath, my lords, and killed Tudḫaliya.

Gods, my lords, you protected(?) my father … […] … And because Ḫattuša […] by the enemy — the enemy had taken the borders of the land of Ḫatti — [he kept attack]ing it and kept killing them, and of the land of Ḫatti he kept [tak]ing the […]. But he (my father) took the borders away from them and […] them back. Moreover, he also (took?) other surrounding lands in (his) kingship […]. He made the land of Ḫatti thrive, and its borders on this side and on that; under him the whole land of Ḫatti fared well; under him cattle and sheep became numerous; and the deportees whom […] from the enemy land […] thrived as well, and none of them perished. But now, gods, [my lords], you have come and at last avenged on my father that matter of Tudḫaliya the Younger. Because of the blood of Tudḫaliya, my father — and those princes, lords, commanders of thousands (and) dignitaries who had sided (with him) — died because of th[at] matter. And that same matter reached the land of Ḫatti too, and the land of [Ḫatti] also began to die because of the matter. And in the land of Ḫatti, from then onward until now, the plague has grown ever stronger; the land of Ḫatti has been damaged by the plague and has become diminished. And I, Muršili, [your] ser[vant], cannot overcome the agitation, and the anguish in (my) body I cannot […].

… gods, my lords, who … to … — because you were summoned from the assembly to oath (and) witness: when all Ḫattuša swore (the oath) on (his) behalf, they …-ed; but they went (and), because (he was) their sworn lo[rd], […]. [And whi]le, gods, my lords, (you did) not (take up?) that case a second time(?), that blood(shed) was in no way sought out […]. […] … [gods], my lords, (are) supreme(?).

[…] … […] … (they) keep …(?) […] my lords, the oath(?) […] which […] killed their […], and his days […] they have already died. […] … but those who from the house […] […] … and in the land of Ḫatti there is continual dying […] … offence … below(?) […] … his […] to my father because […] … […] … of my father … […] … I have confessed […]; and because my father […] Tudḫaliya […], my father afterwards [performed] the blood ritual (išḫanaš SÍSKUR) on that account. But Ḫattuša did nothing (for itself) […]. I came and I too performed the [blood] ritual; but the land [did n]othing, […] … on behalf of the land they did (not?) do anything.

Now, because the land of Ḫatti has been badly oppressed by the plague and there is continual dying in the land of Ḫatti, […] the matter of Tudḫaliya weighed upon the land; it was confirmed for me by [the god] too, and [concerning it] I made an oracle inquiry. And the oath (sworn by) you, [gods], my lords, (and by) your temples was confirmed (as bearing) upon the land in connection with the plague. So they are performing before you, [gods], my lords, the ritual of the oath, and they purify (themselves?). And I too am paying you, gods, my lords, compensation and an appeasement gift (maškan-) on account of the land's [plag]ue.

Gods, my lords, as for the blood of Tudḫaliya which you are avenging: those who killed Tudḫaliya have paid for the blood, and that blood has moreover finished off the land of Ḫatti as well; the land of Ḫatti has already paid for it too. And because it has now reached me as well, I too am paying for it from my own house with compensation and gift. So let the soul of the gods, my lords, be soothed again! Gods, my lords, have pity on me again, and let me be seen (with favour?) by you! Listen to me as I speak to you: I myself have done nothing evil. Of those who sinned and did evil, no one from that time is (left) any longer; they have already died off. But because the matter of my father has reached me, see, on account of the plague of the land I am giving you, gods, my lords, a gift and making compensation; I am paying you gift and compensation. Gods, my lords, have pity on me again, and let me be seen (with favour?) […]. Because the land of Ḫatti has been damaged by the plague and has become few, those who used to prepare the ḫarši-bread and the libation vessel for you, gods, my lords — the plague has pressed them hard, and they […] from the plague […] … and the dying does not let up at all; there is continual dying. And the few bread-offerers and libation-pourers who … — if they perish, then no one will give you thick bread and libation any more.

[…] [my lo]rds, on account of the thick bread and libation which … […] … take (pity?), and let me be seen (with favour?) by you, and [send away(?)] the pl[ague] […]! And these few bread-offerers and [libation-pourers] who [remain(?)] — let them no longer be damaged, let them not d[ie]; let them prepare thick bread and libation for you. Gods, my lords, … send the plague away! And whatever evils … on account of Tudḫaliya have arisen within the land of Ḫatti, gods, … send them off; send them into the enemy's land! But take pi[ty] on the land of Ḫatti, and let (things) become good again in the land. And as for me, your priest, your servant, let me be seen (with favour?) by you. Have pity on me: send the agitation away from my heart, and take the anguish from my body!
[Colophon:] […] Complete. How Muršili made a plea […] on account of the plague […].
